items.title: Harry Shum Jr. Reacts to 'DWTS' Elimination, 'Bullying' Throughout Season
items.summary:
Harry Shum Jr. is speaking out after being sent home from Dancing With the Stars just one week shy of the finale.

“I oddly feel at ease. I don’t feel sad — it’s really weird,” Shum, 44, told E! News after the season 35 semifinals on Tuesday, November 17. “I kind of felt like we accomplished everything we wanted to.”

Shum and pro Jenna Johnson earned back-to-back perfect scores on Tuesday night, receiving 10s across the board for their paso doble and quickstep. Their second dance was performed to “Valerie,” a subtle nod to Shum’s late Glee costar Naya Rivera .

“It felt like that song alone meant so much to so many people, and even to us,” he said after the show. “It was a moment where you kind of saw the underdog be able to have the spotlight, and I always remember that feeling.”

'DWTS' Season 35 Finalists Revealed After Jaw-Dropping Elimination 

While Shum stayed optimistic post-elimination, Johnson, 32, admitted she was looking forward to their “really fun” finale plans.

“That’s the part that I’m most heartbroken about,” she told E! News . “We had concocted this incredible journey that the ballroom won’t see this time. But maybe we’ll put it out there somewhere.”

Disney/Eric McCandless 
 The pair also reflected on the “chaotic” conversations online this season, with Johnson joking that the cast is “a bit all trauma bonded.”

“There’s a lot of trauma bond just because this year has been a little crazy,” Shum added, noting that he hopes to “get to know” his competitors more outside of the ballroom. “Social media is a little nuts. I hope they address that at a certain…
items.t: Harry Shum Jr. Reacts to 'DWTS' Elimination, 'Bullying' Throughout Season

items.title: Isaiah Washington Reveals He's Dating Someone New After Wife's Death
items.summary:
Grey’s Anatomy alum Isaiah Washington has found love again after his wife’s sudden death. 

“I have known many incredible women in my life, but not a single one of them can hold a candle to the deep Southern charm of @keibenet,” Washington, 63, wrote via Instagram on Monday, November 16.

Washington reflected on how he met Kei Benett , adding, “I am not only thrilled to have gotten to know her in the last 9 months talking to her for hours every single day. I am absolutely baffled how any man in her past could have harmed her, belittled her, disrespected her, or even betrayed her in the most deplorable ways.”

In his social media post, Washington gushed over their connection.

Isaiah Washington and Wife Jenisa's Relationship Timeline Before Her Death 

“She has an incredible mind, heart, and spirit and I have grown to respect her intelligence, green thumb, hair stylist talent, entrepreneurship, holistic approach, and her black business owner’s business acumen immensely,” he wrote. “Yes, she has earned her place at my creative table and I love her dearly. I am so glad that all of the men who treated her like she was less than a Queen, all left her heartbroken, but not broken.”

He concluded: “Don’t worry I will take it from here and I will never let her down as a friend and partner in love and creativity. There has been no other woman who has made me laugh and has encouraged me as she has. Yeah, I don’t play about Kei Bennett, and just know that she doesn’t play about me. Yeah … she is all mine now and I am all hers. Deal with it. Expect great things to come from both of us…

items.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger Shares His Secret to Staying Young at 79
items.summary:
Arnold Schwarzenegger is sharing his candid thoughts on aging.

“I don’t think that you have the time, nor do I have the time, to go through the list,” the Terminator actor, 79, told Woman’s World in a cover story published on Wednesday, November 18, when asked what he “could no longer do that he could at 29.”

While the outlet noted that Schwarzenegger is “more cautious about physical risks” these days after years of weightlifting and movie stunts took a toll on his body, he’s not ready to give up on his workout routines completely.

“The training keeps us going,” he shared. “When I leave this gym, everything turns into a — it goes from black and white to a color movie. The whole world looks different afterwards.”

Schwarzenegger also noted the importance of staying connected to others.

“We need human contact. It’s the thing that makes you happy,” he shared.

Chris Pratt Reveals His Unusual Christmas Gift From Arnold Schwarzenegger 

Another thing that brings Schwarzenegger pride and joy is being a grandfather . His and ex Maria Shriver ’s daughter Katherine Schwarzenegger shares three children of her own with husband Chris Pratt : Lyla, 6, Eloise, 4, and Ford, 2. (Arnold and Shriver, 71, also share kids Christina , 35, and Patrick , 33. Meanwhile, the actor is also a dad to son Joseph , 29, with Mildred Baena .)

“I’m so impressed by what great parents Katherine and Chris are,” Arnold, whom Woman’s World crowned its first-ever World’s Hottest Grandpa, told the magazine. (Katherine, 36, and Pratt, 47, tied the knot in 2019.)

Comparing being a grandfather — or an Opa,…
items.t: Arnold Schwarzenegger Shares His Secret to Staying Young at 79

items.title: Mormon Wives' Mayci Neeley 'Embarrassed' Over 'F*** Them Up' Text Message
items.summary:
Mayci Neeley is taking accountability for her actions.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star caused a stir during season 1 of spinoff show The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County when she inserted herself into drama between her sister and Mormon Wives OC cast member, McCall DaPron , and costar Bobbi Althoff .

In a text message shown on screen, Mayci, 31, wrote to friend Jen Affleck , “These girls making my sister… I’m gonna f*** them up.”

But in a video shared via her Instagram Stories on Tuesday, November 17, the Babymama cofounder admitted that her text to Jen, 27, wasn’t appropriate.

What to Know About ‘Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County’ Spinoff 

“To be honest, I’m embarrassed,” Mayci said. “I’m genuinely embarrassed that I said that. I don’t remember the intention behind it because I know I wasn’t trying to get into a street fight, like a physical fight. It’s genuinely embarrassing. I don’t know why the hell I said that.”

The mom-of-three continued, “I was just seeing red in that moment and I said that. I said that to a friend over text. Did I know that Jen was going to go tell everyone I said that? No. Should I have said that? Absolutely not.”

Mayci added, “I am very sorry I said that. I did regret saying that. That is definitely out of character for me. … I’m just going to be accountable for the things that I was upset with myself for. I’ve apologized for it, and moving on.”

items.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
items.summary:
After years of celebrity interviews, I have learned not to be fooled by the allure of fame. We never really know them – we know what they want us to know

As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.

I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.

items.title: Two courtrooms, one celebrity: how did the Russell Brand case compare with the rape trial next door?
items.summary:
One was a high-profile defendant watched by more than 100 journalists. Another was an unknown man who preyed on a girl almost half his age. Their stories played out minutes apart, one entirely out of the spotlight

What is going on inside Russell Brand’s head as he arrives at court for the start of his rape trial? He sees the dozens of cameras and journalists lined outside Southwark crown court, many of whom have been waiting since before 7am, and he tells himself that the media are all against him. “It seems to me that they believe that I am guilty, and that this should be the rubber-stamping of the process of my destruction.”

He walks with his wife, Laura, and his bodyguard past the photographers, “clickering, clackering, snickering paparazzi, like locusts, peculiar concoctions, not fully humans”, and up into the court, where he is suddenly overwhelmed by “the presence of something very beautiful, grace”. “In a situation like I’m in, it’s impossible not to turn to God. Truth and justice are the only things that can save me,” he thinks.
